markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged Skeleton & Muscles readings (elbow angle with the muscle contracting, e.g. 'biceps contracting gave 55 degrees; triceps gave 165 degrees') as evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine readings consistent with the student's own Investigation Record rows; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('the arm bent') with no actual logged numbers quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that muscles work in pairs: the biceps contracts (pulls) to bend the elbow while the triceps relaxes, and the triceps contracts to straighten it while the biceps relaxes, because a muscle can only pull.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement of one contracting while its partner relaxes, with contraction as pulling.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying both muscles contract at the same time, or that muscles push.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that the elbow can only move backward and forward because it is a hinge joint (like a door hinge); ligaments hold the bones together at the joint.
markingScheme.accept: Hinge joint named with its one-direction movement; ligaments are a creditable addition.
markingScheme.insufficient: Naming the joint only as 'a joint', or calling the elbow a ball-and-socket joint.

markingScheme.criterion: Applies one correct job of the skeleton to football: support (holds up the body), protection (e.g. the skull protects the brain, ribs protect the heart and lungs), levers for movement, or marrow making blood cells.
markingScheme.accept: Any one correct skeletal function linked to playing football.
markingScheme.insufficient: A skeletal job stated with no link to football, or an incorrect function.

markingScheme.criterion: Applies one correct job of the muscles to football: skeletal muscles pulling on bones in pairs to run and kick, or the cardiac muscle keeping the heart pumping without tiring.
markingScheme.accept: Any one correct muscle function linked to playing football.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'muscles make you strong' with no mechanism.

markingScheme.criterion: Gives two safety guidelines, each with a correct reason: e.g. warm up (prepares muscles and joints and prevents injury), wear protective gear/helmet (protects the skull and bones), listen to your body (prevents overuse injury), stay active regularly (keeps the heart and joints healthy).
markingScheme.accept: Two different guidelines each with a sensible reason; both needed for the mark.
markingScheme.insufficient: One guideline only, or guidelines with no reasons.
